source.title: Mixture-of-Experts Models in Vision: Routing, Optimization, and Generalization
source.authors: Adam Rokah; Daniel S. Veress; Caleb Caulk; S. Sharan

record.file_problem: Supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares MoE and dense classifier heads on natural CIFAR-10 labels and reports accuracy and curvature measurements. It does not test any listed version: there is no random-label comparison, width sweep, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout test, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training and validation accuracy and Hessian statistics. It also describes loss-surface perturbation results in text and a figure, but does not give numerical values for those perturbations. Routing and efficiency results do not bear on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares dense and MoE classifier heads sharing a ResNet-18 backbone. It tests none of V1–V8: natural-label fitting alone does not test V1, and its unscaled Hessian statistics and eigenvector perturbations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. It also cites the large-batch original but performs no batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: appropriately regularized MoE models attain perfect training accuracy and comparable validation performance, with small validation gains over Dense; curvature and routing-sensitive perturbation diagnostics do not directly explain predictive performance. Qualify the curvature statement: SoftMoE is highest on test-set Hessian metrics, whereas its training-set metrics are lower than Dense's. The authors also conclude that naive sparse routing provides no practical inference speedup in this setting.
record.recipe_differences: Image classification with matched-capacity ResNet-18-based dense, SoftMoE, and SparseMoE classifier heads; SGD with momentum and weight decay. No listed original method is reproduced.

fits_no_version.finding: All three architectures attain 100% maximum training accuracy. Peak validation accuracies are 87.86% for Dense, 88.24% for SoftMoE, and 88.16% for SparseMoE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the study's matched-capacity CIFAR-10 recipe, MoE classifier heads attain slightly higher peak validation accuracy than a dense head sharing the same ResNet-18 backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: SoftMoE has higher test-set Hessian eigenvalue and trace than Dense despite slightly higher peak validation accuracy. On training data, both MoE models have lower Hessian statistics than Dense.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across these three architectures, the relationship between unscaled Hessian curvature and validation accuracy depends on the evaluation split and curvature statistic.

record.problems: The study reports one dataset and a controlled set of three classifier heads. It gives no uncertainty estimates for the accuracy or Hessian values. Validation accuracy is reported, while the text does not provide numerical test accuracy. Hessian statistics are diagnostics distinct from the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Figure 7 describes qualitative loss changes under perturbations but supplies no numerical values; the paper says those curves primarily capture global routing effects rather than local flatness.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or random-label held-out evaluation establishes coexistence under the same training recipe.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
All models share a convolutional backbone; dense versus MoE classifier heads is not convolutional versus fully connected image learning.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget comparison; all models use momentum SGD.
No training batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, ranking of generalization gaps within one convolutional family, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are warranted for the listed versions. The reported validation values are selection maxima, and numerical final test accuracy is not supplied. Figure 7 is already declared in rows_left_out and does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. No uncertainty estimates establish whether the small validation differences are reproducible.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbation measure or comparison of its ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
